articles.headline: Higher Ground: How New York is raising a park to hold back the sea
articles.summary: On 29 October 2012, Hurricane Sandy slammed into New York City, unleashing a devastating storm surge that flooded homes, subways and tunnels, knocked out power and sparked deadly fires.&nbsp;

articles.headline: Ocean’s ability to absorb carbon is weakening as climate change intensifies, UN warns
articles.summary: The ocean absorbs around 30 per cent of human-caused carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions and 90 per cent of excess heat trapped by greenhouse gases. But climate change has already reduced its capacity to absorb carbon by approximately six per cent, a new UN report warns ahead of th...

articles.headline: Nepal’s deadly glacier flood a ‘defining moment’ for the international community
articles.summary: The deadly flash flood that tore through Nepal in August is a “defining moment” for both the country and the international community, according to the head of the UN field agency which builds roads, schools and clinics in crisis zones.

articles.headline: In the Mekong Delta, a push to grow food with saltwater
articles.summary: For generations, farming in Viet Nam’s Mekong Delta has depended on a delicate bargain. The river flooded, retreated and flooded again, carrying freshwater and sediment across a flat landscape whose vast fields helped turn the country into one of the world’s leading rice expor...

articles.headline: Amid heartache of Nepal flooding disaster, fear remains
articles.summary: Six weeks after Nepal’s deadly flooding disaster, communities are still struggling to rebuild their lives,&nbsp;but they will need sustained help as global warming increases the risk of another Himalayan catastrophe, the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) said on Friday.&nbsp;

articles.headline: ‘Overshoot is not a reason to surrender’: UN calls for accelerated climate action ahead of COP31 summit
articles.summary: As world leaders prepare for November’s major&nbsp;COP31 climate summit in Türkiye, record-breaking heat, devastating floods and an unprecedented El Niño climate pattern are making global climate action ever more urgent.

articles.headline: From drought to deluge: ‘Super’ El Niño’s expanding reach
articles.summary: Across Papua New Guinea, water sources are drying up, crops are failing and food prices are rising months before the worst agricultural impacts are expected. Behind those warning signs is an El Niño whose Pacific Ocean temperatures have already surpassed the equivalent measure...

articles.headline: ‘Rising seas are sinking futures’
articles.summary: World leaders approved the UN Declaration on Sea Level Rise by consensus on Thursday as the UN chief warned that encroaching waters are already threatening the future of coastal communities worldwide.

articles.headline: LIVE: Climate change is here - What happens next is still in our hands
articles.summary: From deadly floods in the Himalayas to wildfires and extreme heat across Europe, 2026 has brought a succession of stark reminders of a changing climate. The task is immediate: Protect people from the impacts already unfolding while rapidly cutting the emissions of harmful gass...

articles.headline: When a country goes underwater: Island States fight for their future
articles.summary: Rising sea levels and ever-more-powerful storms are eroding shorelines, submerging land and threatening to evict millions of people from their homes worldwide.&nbsp;

articles.headline: How El Niño offers a test of whether the world can adapt to a changing climate
articles.summary: El Niño is strengthening in a world that is already hotter, raising the risk of drought, floods and crop losses across some of the world’s most important food-producing regions. But unlike many disasters, this one can be seen coming. UN experts say the months ahead offer count...

articles.headline: In Tanzania, the sea is moving inland – and taking livelihoods with it
articles.summary: Along the coast of Tanzania, in East Africa, the Indian Ocean is pushing saltwater ever farther inland, shrinking coconut harvests, driving fish away and leaving some residents wondering how much longer they can stay.

articles.headline: UN-Water Global Report: Valuing Water in a Changing Climate and Growing Scarcity
articles.summary: The United Nations World Water Development Report highlights that over 2 billion people experience high water stress. The report urges nations to reform wastewater treatment, safeguard wetlands, and implement integrated water resources management (IWRM).

articles.headline: DENR-EMB Intensifies River Water Quality Monitoring Across Manila Bay Tributaries
articles.summary: The Philippine Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) and Environmental Management Bureau (EMB) deployed automated biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) stations along the Pasig, Marikina, and Tullahan river systems to track industrial effluent compliance under RA 9275.
articles.publisher: Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR)

articles.headline: UNEP and Marine Scientists Document Resilience in the Coral Triangle Despite Heatwaves
articles.summary: New findings from the United Nations Environment Programme indicate that strictly protected marine sanctuaries in the Coral Triangle, including Tubbataha and Apo Reef, show higher thermal resilience due to enforced no-take zones and reduced terrestrial runoff.

articles.headline: WHO/UNICEF JMP Report: Accelerating Household Water Safety and Hygiene Access
articles.summary: The latest Joint Monitoring Programme update reveals that improving household point-of-use filtration and eliminating micro-leaks can save up to 35% of potable domestic water while significantly curbing waterborne pathogens in suburban communities.

articles.headline: World Resources Institute: Aqueduct Water Risk Atlas Identifies Critical Watersheds
articles.summary: WRI data shows 25 countries face extremely high water stress each year, regularly using up to 80% of their renewable water supply. The research advocates for watershed reforestation, urban rainwater harvesting, and smart metering.

articles.headline: DENR Launches Integrated Watershed Rehabilitation for Angat and Ipo Basins
articles.summary: To safeguard Metro Manila’s primary water reservoir, the DENR partnered with local indigenous communities and water concessionaires to plant native hardwood species across 5,000 hectares of degraded buffer lands.

articles.headline: UN Intergovernmental Negotiating Committee Advances Global Treaty on Plastic Pollution
articles.summary: Delegates from 170 nations negotiate binding targets to stop synthetic polymers and single-use microplastics from suffocating freshwater rivers and coastal marine nurseries before 2040.

articles.headline: NOAA Coral Reef Watch Confirms Widespread Bleaching Across Equatorial Reefs
articles.summary: Satellite heat anomaly data indicates elevated thermal stress across the Indian, Pacific, and Atlantic basins. Marine biologists emphasize rapid local water quality improvements as vital to reduce coral vulnerability.

articles.headline: IPCC Working Group: Climate Change Directly Intensifies Global Hydrological Cycles
articles.summary: Climate modeling from the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change confirms that every 0.5°C temperature rise increases heavy precipitation events by 7% while simultaneously worsening dry-season soil moisture deficits.

articles.headline: Philippine Clean Water Act: DENR Cites 2 Decades of Industrial Effluent Standards
articles.summary: Marking milestones in Philippine water jurisprudence, the DENR highlighted the impact of Republic Act 9275 in shutting down illegal industrial dischargers and promoting wastewater recycling in food and beverage factories.

articles.headline: Health in all policies: the case of air pollution, urban health and sustainability
